newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle close slightly lower.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle close slightly lower.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed slightly lower amid some concern that recent run-ups in both cash cattle and beef markets may be poised to stall.
"It looks like (retail meat) buyers are starting to pick up more chicken and pork because of the run-up in the beef," said analyst Joe Kropf of Kropf and Love Consulting.
USDA boxed beef cut-out values, as of 1130 CDT, were down $0.18 to $0.01 per cwt for choice cuts, with 47 fabricated loads traded.
Floor sources said R.J. O'Brien was a featured seller of August with Cargill Investor Services a noted buyer.
August live cattle closed off 0.225 cent at 67.30 cents a lb. Other months were down 0.450 to 0.075 cent.

Cash cattle trade was at a virtual standstill. There was growing sentiment that trade will develop this week at a steady $66 per cwt. Late last week many had expected trade this week would be up $1 at $67.

Feeder cattle futures also closed lower with some traders seeing signs of a reversal in the market's five-month uptrend, which took August to a contract high of 83.40 cents a lb in late July. August closed off 0.625 cent at 80.90 cents with other months down 0.450 to 0.200 cent.

Dealers said recent strength in corn prices had helped make feeder cattle buyers nervous. CBOT corn closed lower Monday but new crop futures prices remain around 30 cents a bushel higher than those trading about a month ago.
The latest CME feeder index, for August 1, was up $0.19 at $82.56.
